newsitem.title: USA: Unison aims for 88 percent occupancy rate.
newsitem.headline: Unison aims for 88 percent occupancy rate.

text.p: Unison Healthcare Corp President and Chief Executive Officer Jerry Walker said the company "appears to be well on its way" toward achieving an 88 percent occupancy level in its assisted living facilities.

Speaking at the Cruttenden Roth Growth Stock Conference here, Walker said last year's average occupancy rate of about 82.1 percent was lower than the industry average. He blamed this figure on Unison's presense in Texas and Indiana, two states where industrywide occupancy levels are among the lowest in the nation.
Unison, whose revenues grew from $61.3 million in 1995 to an estimated $154.3 million in 1996, is expanding at a rate of about two to three new facilities per month, Walker said.
"I don't know if it's possible to continue to double revenues," he said. "But there is no impediment to doing this in terms of our access to capital and the quality of acquisition opportunities."
The company has grown from 20 assisted living facilities in 1994 to 59 by the end of last year.
Walker said future expansion will be targeted in medium-sized rural communities rather than large urban markets.
